reading.title: The Saturday Book Swap
reading.purpose: Follow two friends as they run a neighborhood book swap and solve a rainy-day problem.
paras: Devon and Mei planned a sidewalk book swap to raise money for new park benches. They set up three folding tables at dawn. Because of a warm breeze, early walkers stopped right away to browse the shelves.

Mei sorted picture books by topic. Meanwhile, at the very same time, Devon counted out change and taped up bright signs. For example, one sign pointed directly to animal mysteries, and another marked sports stories. In addition, they offered free bookmarks that Mei had painted the night before.

Around noon, dark clouds rolled in and heavy rain began to fall. As a result, the cardboard boxes started to soak through. They could not leave the books outside; therefore, for that reason, they hurried to carry every crate into the community center gym.

The dry gym felt calm and cozy. In contrast, on the completely different side of the glass doors, the sidewalk looked empty and gray. Furthermore, the gym had wide benches where readers could sit and sample chapters.

Eventually, after a long afternoon of steady rain, the skies cleared. Every single book found a new home, and afterward, once the tables were folded, Devon and Mei walked to the park to pick out the best spot for the new bench.

choices: at the very same time as another action
after the rain stopped later in the afternoon
because of a warm morning breeze on the street
for the exact reason that a box got soaked
qs.why: Paragraph 2 explains meanwhile with the clue "at the very same time" as Mei sorted books and Devon counted change.

qs.q: Which sentence shows what happened to the boxes when the rain started?
choices: Around noon, dark clouds rolled in and heavy rain began to fall.
As a result, the cardboard boxes started to soak through.
The dry gym felt calm and cozy.
Every single book found a new home, and afterward, once the tables were folded, Devon and Mei walked to the park to pick out the best spot for the new bench.
qs.why: This sentence states the direct effect of the rain on the cardboard boxes.

ev.text: As a result, the cardboard boxes started to soak through.

qs.q: Why did moving into the gym turn out to be helpful?
choices: The gym was dry and gave readers benches to sit on.
The gym had brand-new cardboard boxes ready to hold all the wet signs.
The gym was right next to the park where they wanted to build a bench.
The gym stayed open all night so Devon could paint extra bookmarks.
qs.why: Paragraph 4 says the gym was dry, calm, and cozy, and it had wide benches where readers could sit and sample chapters.

qs.q: What is this story mostly about?
choices: How to paint bookmarks and sort animal mysteries for a school library
Why rainy Saturdays usually ruin outdoor sales in a neighborhood park
Two friends who adapt to rain and run a successful book swap
How community centers decide where to place folding tables and benches
qs.why: Devon and Mei organize the book swap, move indoors when rain hits, and succeed in finding a home for every book.
